title: The Last Sigil Again
premise: Odile Eriksen, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a charm-seller in the magic-free city of Vellharrow, discovers that a century-old book of prophecies has recorded tonight's date — and that the man he's meeting for dinner is written into it as his doom. The prophecy names him 'the thief who returns,' and when the court beneath Mount Sarn claims the soul of his date, Tomas, as payment for an old bargain Odile's family made, Odile must descend into the mountain to steal it back. Along the way he recovers memories the exile stripped from him: he was not banished for calling storms, but for selling his own name to buy someone else's life. In the end, Odile trades his last sigil — the mark of who he was — to free Tomas's soul, choosing to become no one in particular rather than the person the prophecy required, and the two walk out of the mountain into a storm he can no longer call but can finally stand inside.
about_author: August Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people whose pasts arrive with interest due.

chapters.title: The Date on Page 114
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Closing his charm stall at dusk, Odile meets Tomas for their first real dinner — then finds tonight's exact date inscribed in a prophetic ledger he bought years ago and never dared read fully. The entry names two men and a debt. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread; the ordinary evening becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Charms Without Magic
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Flashback woven through present: seven years selling inert trinkets in Vellharrow, where the Wardens burn anything that hums. Odile examines the ledger's language and recognizes his mother's dialect — this book came from home. Beat: loneliness sharpened by recognition.

chapters.title: What Tomas Knows
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas admits he sought Odile out deliberately: his grandmother left him a letter naming 'the storm-caller' as the only one who could help when the mountain came for him. He shows the letter; it bears the Eriksen seal. Beat: betrayal braided with tenderness — Odile realizes the date wasn't chance.

chapters.title: The Warden's Knock
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Wardens raid the market after someone reports a humming charm. Odile hides the ledger, watches a neighbor's stall burned, and understands someone informed on him specifically. Beat: fear and guilt; the safe city was never safe.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain, A Ledger of Souls
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. That night Tomas dreams of Mount Sarn's under-court: a hall where souls are filed like deeds. He wakes with frost on his window shaped into a summons. Beat: awe and violation; the dream knows his name.

chapters.title: Seven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A full flashback: the trial, the stripping of his name, the sentence of exile — and the memory the rite failed to erase, of a younger sister he saved by signing something. Beat: grief surfacing; the reader learns the exile was a purchase.

chapters.title: The Bargain of Eriksen
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Deciphering the letter with Odile, they learn Tomas's grandmother bought her son's life from the under-court using an Eriksen co-signature — a debt now maturing, payable in the next generation's soul. Beat: horror at inherited contracts; anger at the dead.

chapters.title: Running Out of Sky
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Frost-signs spread across Vellharrow; the mountain is collecting early. Odile tries a small working to slow it and his old sigil flares visible on his wrist — the Wardens will see it soon. Beat: desperation; hiding is over.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. They trace the tip to Maren, Odile's only friend, who confesses she reported him to protect her own daughter, whose name also appears in the ledger. Beat: painful empathy; everyone in the city is collateral.

chapters.title: Down Is the Only Door
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Rather than wait for arrest or collection, Odile chooses to go to the mountain voluntarily, taking the ledger as both map and weapon. Tomas insists on coming. Beat: resolve replacing flight; the descent begins.

chapters.title: The Stair of Names
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Inside Mount Sarn, a stair carved with every name ever surrendered. Odile finds his own name half-eroded and reads what was written beneath it — not 'storm-caller' but 'debtor.' Beat: identity shaken; the mountain remembers him differently than he does.

chapters.title: Court of Quiet Things
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. They reach the under-court: magistrates of ash and patience who do not shout because they never need to. The court offers terms — Tomas's soul, or an equivalent already owed. Beat: cold terror; bureaucracy as horror.

chapters.title: The Equivalent Already Owed
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The equivalent is Odile himself: the court holds his original contract, and his exile was merely deferral. He can pay with his memory-self — everything he is — and keep Tomas whole. Beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: Maren Descends
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren follows them down with her daughter's ledger page, intending to bargain separately and damn them both if needed. She witnesses the court's true scale and falters. Beat: cowardice cracking into conscience.

chapters.title: What the Sigil Was For
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the court's archive, Odile reads his full contract and learns the truth: his sigil isn't a brand but a receipt — proof he once paid a soul's price, and it can be spent once more, entirely. Beat: revelation; the mark of shame is actually currency.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Prophecy
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The court produces its own copy of the century-old prophecy and reads the ending aloud: 'the thief who returns will leave with nothing of himself.' Tomas realizes the prophecy never said Odile dies — it said he forgets. Beat: dread refined into clarity.

chapters.title: Terms Refused
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile refuses both offered terms and instead contests the contract itself, invoking an archaic clause: a debt signed under a false name is void. But proving it means revealing the false name — his sister's, which he took. Beat: defiance at great cost.

chapters.title: The Sister in the Stair
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The court summons the co-signatory: Odile's sister, alive, serving out her purchased years as the court's record-keeper. Their reunion is a wound — she chose servitude believing he'd forgotten her. Beat: devastating tenderness; the theme of memory made flesh.

chapters.title: Storm-Caller, No Longer
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Climax. To void the contract, Odile spends the sigil — surrendering his name, his craft, and every memory of why he did any of it. The court's hall cracks; the mountain exhales a hundred years of held weather. Beat: sacrifice as climax; he wins by becoming no one.

chapters.title: Souls Returned
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. With the contract voided, the court must release all souls held under Eriksen signatures — including Tomas's and Maren's daughter's claim. The exodus up the stair of names, each reclaimed soul speaking its own name aloud. Beat: catharsis; restoration without erasure.

chapters.title: A Man Without a Name
chapters.summary: Odile's POV (thin, fragmentary). Odile wakes above ground remembering nothing — not the mountain, not the cost, barely himself. Tomas tells him none of it, keeping only the ledger closed beside them. Beat: bittersweet quiet; love persisting without testimony.

chapters.title: The Storm He Can Stand In
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, converging. Rain comes to Vellharrow for the first time in seven years, and Odile stands in it feeling inexplicably at home. His sister arrives at the stall door, and though he doesn't know her, he doesn't look away. Beat: belonging rebuilt from scratch; memory lost, identity chosen.
